column9: Digital Mourning as Collective Psychosocial Support: A Descriptive Phenomenology of Technologically Mediated Grief in a Collectivist Context
column10: This study examines digital mourning as collective psychosocial support in a collectivist context. column9: A BRIEF PRIMER OF SOCIAL COGNITION FOR FORENSIC PSYCHOLOGY
column10: This chapter will provide a general overview of the social cognitive approach and of how broader models of person perception can be applied within the area of forensic, offence-related perceptions. Social cognitive bias will be introduced to the reader in detail including schemas and their accessibility and the dual-process model. The reader will then be introduced to how social cognition operates across forensic contexts in terms of person perception (i.e., defendant, those who offend, and eyewitness perception). Particular attention is paid regarding how social cognition across the forensic context can limit decision-making, and suggestions for future research and practice are made.
